presets.label: Thorough (recommended recipe)
presets.blurb: The recipe that was tested: two stages, the first on 40 M tokens and the last on the recipe's 40 or 80 M, full thinking checks, a check of every cut, a retry and a back-off when a thinking check fails.
presets.risk: No shortcut. The only risk is the cut itself.

presets.label: Balanced
presets.blurb: Two stages, a lighter first stage (20 M tokens), the same sequence length in both stages so the original writes its answers only once, quick thinking checks (16 questions) and a quick Try first. The last stage keeps the recipe's tokens.
presets.risk: The first stage learns half as much and the quick checks are noisier. Runs that healed below the recipe have failed the thinking checks before; the checks will tell, and a failed check costs a retry.

presets.label: Fast (quick look)
presets.blurb: One stage on 20 M tokens, quick checks, no check of the unhealed cut, no retry, no back-off and no importance matrix.
presets.risk: Far below the recipe: a model that thinks will very likely lose its reasoning. Use it to see roughly how a cut behaves, not to keep the result.

presets.label: Stop early when good (periodic checks, experimental)
presets.blurb: Balanced, but every stage heals in rounds of 5 M tokens with a quick thinking check after each round (not before 10 M) and stops at the first round that passes, then checks the merged model. The cap stays the recipe's tokens. Experimental: nobody has measured yet whether healing in rounds ends as good as one long heal.
presets.risk: A quick check asks 16 questions, so one or two answers decide pass or fail; the merged model is checked again at the end and decides. Every round costs about 25 minutes of loading and checking, so a run that never passes takes a few hours longer than Balanced. Whether rounds reach the quality of one long heal is not known yet.

presets.label: Custom
presets.blurb: Your own choice in the advanced speed settings below.
presets.risk: Whatever you set below the recipe is listed in the plan and the report.
